channel.title: Texas Legislature - Today's Filed Bills in the Senate
channel.description: Bills filed on 11/10/2026. An appearance of a bill on this list is a result of it being filed by a representative or senator.

item.title: SB 310 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Rehmet | Cook, Molly
item.description: Relating to the public school finance system.

item.title: SB 311 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to employment verification of certain health facility applicants.

item.title: SB 312 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the authority of the Health and Human Services Commission's office of the ombudsman to resolve complaints against the Department of Family and Protective Services.

item.title: SB 313 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to a "Texas solution" to reforming and addressing issues related to the Medicaid program, including the creation of an alternative program designed to ensure health benefit plan coverage to certain low-income individuals through the private marketplace; requiring a fee.

item.title: SB 314 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the continuation of a health care provider participation program by the Harris County Hospital District.

item.title: SB 315 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the operability of elevators and related equipment following a power outage at a senior independent living community; authorizing an administrative penalty.

item.title: SB 316 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the creation of an oversight advisory council on foster care placement.

item.title: SB 317 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to required generators or other power sources for certain housing developments that receive an allocation of low income housing tax credits.

item.title: SB 318 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to a prohibition on payments for health care provider referrals to certain unlicensed group homes; creating a criminal offense.

item.title: SB 319 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the maintenance of criminal history record information for group home applicants and employees; creating a criminal offense.

item.title: SB 320 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to power duration requirements in emergency contingency plans adopted by end stage renal disease facilities.

item.title: SB 321 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to an action to remedy certain conditions affecting safety or habitability of certain residential rental property; providing a civil penalty.

item.title: SB 322 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to requiring the Texas Commission on Law Enforcement to study and report on incidents of racial profiling.

item.title: SB 323 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the creation of the office of independent oversight ombudsman for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.

item.title: SB 324 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to the enforcement of municipal rules, ordinances, or police regulations prohibiting illegal dumping; increasing a penalty.

item.title: SB 325 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Miles
item.description: Relating to air quality permits for certain concrete plants and crushing facilities.

item.title: SB 326 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Gutierrez
item.description: Relating to the establishment of the Texas automobile insurance public option.

item.title: SB 327 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Gutierrez | Menéndez
item.description: Relating to prohibiting the transfer of certain semiautomatic rifles to certain recipients younger than 21 years of age; creating a criminal offense; increasing a criminal penalty.

item.title: SB 328 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Huffman
item.description: Relating to the operation near a public or private primary or secondary school or a preschool of a retail establishment selling vaping apparatuses or tobacco products; providing a civil penalty.

item.title: SB 329 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Hagenbuch
item.description: Relating to creating the criminal offense of trespass on or near school or day-care center property.

item.title: SB 330 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Zaffirini
item.description: Relating to an exemption from sales and use taxes for certain items listed by the comptroller of public accounts and sold on Veterans Day.

item.title: SB 331 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Paxton
item.description: Relating to the remote participation of certain persons in a proceeding for the issuance or modification of a protective order.

item.title: SB 332 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Paxton
item.description: Relating to timely billing requirements for health care service providers.

item.title: SB 333 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Blanco
item.description: Relating to required provision of workers' compensation insurance coverage for employees of building and construction contractors and subcontractors.

item.title: SB 334 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Menéndez
item.description: Relating to requirements for a court order following a permanency hearing for a child in the conservatorship of the Department of Family and Protective Services.

item.title: SB 335 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Menéndez
item.description: Relating to the best interest of the child in a suit affecting the parent-child relationship.

item.title: SB 336 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Menéndez
item.description: Relating to health benefit plan coverage of treatments for pediatric neuroinflammatory disease.

item.title: SB 337 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Menéndez
item.description: Relating to mail theft and certain criminal offenses committed against an employee or contractor of a common carrier or delivery service delivering mail; increasing criminal penalties.

item.title: SCR 2 Introduced
item.dc:creator: Paxton
item.description: Urging Congress to propose and send to the states for ratification a constitutional amendment to clarify that the states and Congress, within their respective jurisdictions, may reasonably regulate and limit the spending of money to influence campaigns, elections, or ballot measures.
